outcome: Read and understand a range of prose fiction, including texts met for the first time.
Find and interpret themes, ideas and information in good-quality writing.
Read in different ways for different purposes and judge how useful, relevant and well presented a text is.
Draw inferences and back them up with evidence; support a point of view by pointing to the text.
Spot bias and misuse of evidence, telling supported statements from unsupported ones.
Reflect critically on a text using its context and wider reading, and accept that readers can respond differently.
Identify the main theme or themes and summarise ideas and information from a single text.
Explain how vocabulary and grammar make a text effective, using linguistic and literary terms accurately.
Analyse and evaluate how form and structure add to a text's impact.
Write accurately and effectively to describe, narrate, explain, instruct, give and respond to information, and argue.
Choose vocabulary, grammar, form and structure to suit audience, purpose and context.
Use language imaginatively and creatively, drawing on information provided by others to write in different forms.
Keep a consistent point of view and stay coherent and consistent across the whole text.
Select, organise and emphasise facts, ideas and key points.
Use evidence and quotation well to support views, and create emotional impact.
Use persuasive language and rhetorical devices such as rhetorical questions, antithesis and parenthesis.
